newsitem.title: CHINA: China said to end credit quotas for state banks.
newsitem.headline: China said to end credit quotas for state banks.

text.p: China's central bank plans to phase out credit quotas for its four major state banks from 1997 to accelerate their transformation into commercial banks, the Economic Information News said on Wednesday.
The four banks are the Construction Bank, Bank of China, the Industrial and Commercial Bank and the Agricultural Bank.

The central bank has already started ending the quotas on an experimental basis for some banks, such as those in Shanghai, and allowing them to lend on the basis of their reserves and debt-to-equity ratio, the newspaper said.
The central bank wants to stop a rise in policy loans by state banks that cause inflation, it said but gave no more details.
Officials of the central bank could not be immediately reached for comment.
Credit quotas have been a major instrument of Beijing's financial policy control since 1949.
